text:
sara-cs: Heads up — AcmeRetail reported that their reranking scores flipped after yesterday's model push. They sent a repro payload where the same query + candidates that used to order candidate X above Y now shows Y > X and their UX metrics dropped. Customer is on slack support thread and is pretty unhappy. They pasted sample requests and before/after scores.

miguel-eng: can you drop the sample here? also which model variant did we promote?

sara-cs: pasted below. They were using our rerank endpoint with model `rerank-v2` (default alias). We rolled a small patch to rerank-v2 around 05:12 UTC (deploy-bot shows 1764006721) that included a quantization kernel tweak for int8. Repro payload:

```json
{
  "query": "best winter running shoes for narrow feet",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"A","text":"Trail shoe with narrow fit"},
    {"id":"B","text":"Lightweight road runner, narrow"},
    {"id":"C","text":"Winterized boot with insulation"}
  ],
  "top_k": 3
}
```

Their baseline scores (pre-deploy): A: 0.78, B: 0.62, C: 0.11
New scores (post-deploy): A: 0.61, B: 0.65, C: 0.12

anya-ml: interesting — these are same inputs, same tokenization? any whitespace/normalization differences?

sara-cs: Customer says they used exact same JSON; they recorded request body hash and it's identical. No client changes.

kevin-runtime: I pulled the model artifact used for the deploy and ran the same request locally against the runtime with --deterministic flag. I got A:0.78, B:0.62. So locally it matches baseline.

miguel-eng: so it's not model weights? Could be routing to a different fallback model variant in prod due to the kernel tweak (we added a compatibility alias). Maybe some shards are still serving quantized variant.

kevin-runtime: checked host labels: traffic is split between rerank-v2.float32 and rerank-v2.int8 (we enabled gradual promotion). Host pool shows ~60% int8. I re-ran on an int8 host and got A:0.61, B:0.65 — reproduced.

anya-ml: ok that nails it. int8 quantization changed logits ordering for this input. We need to know if that's widespread or edge-case (numerical instability causing order flips).

miguel-eng: action items: 1) collect failing input set from customer (they provided 20 examples), 2) run our internal eval set across both float32 and int8 to measure swap rate, 3) consider rolling back quantized traffic or pin customer to float32 while we investigate.

sara-cs: I already asked Acme for the full 20-case list. They gave them — uploaded to S3 link: s3://redwood-esc/acme-repro/1764009.zip (private). They want a timeline.

jeff-se: FYI — Acme is mid-enterprise and on a reserved plan. They expect stability. If this persists we should offer to pin them to float32 or credit some invoices.

kevin-runtime: quick diagnostic notes: quantization reduced some logits by ~0.15 on average for candidate A in these queries; ordering flips are happening when score gap < 0.2. Might be expected but we should quantify. Also noticed an order nondeterminism bug in the scoring aggregator we recently changed: when candidate scores tie within 1e-3 we used to stable-sort by candidate id; a previous change inadvertently used unordered map iteration before sorting for some code paths. Could amplify flips across hosts.

miguel-eng: can you show the diff?

kevin-runtime: paste log + mini-diff: 

```diff
- // old: deterministic sort by (score desc, candidate_id asc)
- std::stable_sort(cands.begin(), cands.end(), cmp_score_id);
+ // new: collect scores in unordered_map then sort by score only 
+ // (missed tie-breaker stable sort)
+ std::vector<pair> vec(scores_map.begin(), scores_map.end());
+ std::sort(vec.begin(), vec.end(), cmp_score);
```

kevin-runtime: so two factors: quantization introducing small numeric deltas, and tie-break nondeterminism. Together they cause visible flips.

anya-ml: good catch. Root cause is interaction between quant noise and sorting change. Fix plan: restore stable tie-breaker in aggregator and add unit tests, and run full regression across our eval corpus comparing int8 vs float32 with swap-rate threshold. If swap-rate > X% we should reduce traffic or re-tune quantization.

miguel-eng: immediate mitigation: roll back the aggregator change in prod (hotfix) so sort is stable, and tag workaround for customers until we tune quantization. Also pin Acme to float32 until we remediate.

sara-cs: Acme asked for ETA; can we give a short-term ETA?

kevin-runtime: I can push hotfix to aggregator in the next patch window (30m) and toggle routing to prefer float32 for Acme now.

miguel-eng: I'll run batch eval in background. Anya, can you compute swap-rate metric on the 10k eval set comparing int8 vs float, and return a per-candidate delta histogram?

anya-ml: on it. I'll run it on the eval harness and post a summary in ~2 hours. Early spot-check: swap-rate on 1k dev samples ~0.6% but concentrated in low-margin queries. Will confirm.

sara-cs: I'll tell Acme: we reproduced, found two contributing issues (quantization and sorting change), we're rolling a hotfix for sorting now, and can pin them to float32 immediately. ETA: hotfix in 30m, full eval and follow-up in 2-3 hours. Offering a one-week credit if they want to stay on int8 during fix.

jeff-se: remind legal to prep a short customer note and credit approval path.

deploy-bot: deployment 1764010899: hotfix/restore-stable-sorting -> prod (canary=10%)

kevin-runtime: hotfix deployed to canary hosts, monitoring metrics. Running customer payloads against canary shows A:0.78 again. Rolling to 50% in ~10m.

sara-cs: shared update with Acme — they confirmed canary looks good so far. They want final roll after full eval.

miguel-eng: postmortem actions we should capture: revert unstable aggregator change from PR #3312, add deterministic sorting tests, add int8 vs float32 swap-rate check in our predeploy eval, and update rollout runbook to include fallback pinning per-customer.

anya-ml: will add quantization tuning task to backlog (measure per-layer sensitivity). Also add an automated alert if swap-rate exceeds 0.2% after any model variant promotion.

sara-cs: customers happy for now, they appreciated quick response. I'll keep the thread open until final roll and close after we confirm no regressions across their 20-case set. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
